evidence_test: Reproduction outside the repository (npm 10.9.9, node 22.23.4, linux x64; founder ledger f1041): a lockfileVersion 3 project whose one package has os ["darwin"], hasInstallScript true and scripts.install 'exit 3', unpacked under node_modules as the verifier unpacks every row; `npm --prefix W rebuild --offline --foreground-scripts <name>` runs the script on linux and exits 3 (npm rebuild applies no platform filter; npm ci would not have installed the package). The same with an optional package whose script fails: exit 1. With scripts.install 'node-gyp rebuild' and a binding.gyp: exit 1 with no python on PATH (gyp ERR! find Python), and exit 1 with python present and the headers host unreachable (gyp http GET .../node-v22.23.4-headers.tar.gz, FetchError). What the pages say: 29g:28-30 refuses a fetch unless every package of the lock that has an install script is marked in install_scripts_required (no platform or reachability condition; 29g:17-21 fetches every packages entry but the root, workspace links and workspace folders); 08:20 says the step that needs a script is marked in the recipe and runs offline in kos; 26c:67-70 says what a mark is. No page says whether every marked script must run and succeed, or only those the unit's commands need. This brain's reading (referee/profile/unit_verify.py step 3, accepted and frozen): one offline `npm rebuild` naming every marked row; a nonzero exit refuses the recipe (install_scripts_failed). Measured on the copy target's clone (read only, commit tree 4f479013a42f): all three locks carry such rows. Root lock: 2993 packages entries, 15 with hasInstallScript, among them fsevents 2.3.3 and playwright/node_modules/fsevents 2.3.2 (os darwin, install 'node-gyp rebuild') and cpu-features 0.0.10 (optional, 'node buildcheck.js > buildcheck.gypi && node-gyp rebuild'); the other two locks (582 and 323 entries) carry fsevents too. By Node's lookup over the lock, the lint tools reach 0 of the 15, jest's tools 4 and vitest's 2; the linux-x64 binding packages those need are separate lock entries without scripts. The official node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim image's history names no python, make or g++, and the verifier's runs have no network. So with the pages read this way every unit of this target (18 of 32 package.json directories fit statically) is expected to end install_scripts_failed whatever unit is proposed: an inference from the scratch runs above, not a measurement in the image; cycle 6 measures it on targets/copy/units.json. A lock with fsevents is the common case for a JavaScript repository (it is an optional dependency of the usual file watchers), so the question is general, not this target's. Asked, one line on a page: (1) does a mark mean 'may be fetched although it has a script' or 'its script must run and exit 0 in kos'; (2) are packages whose os/cpu/libc exclude the image's platform fetched and unpacked at all (npm does not install them); (3) does a failing script of an optional package refuse the recipe (npm install tolerates it). The brain's fix follows the answer and waits for the freeze to end (29b: no referee/ change after the exit).
